what: Monolithic Power Systems designs power-management chips: the components that convert and regulate electricity inside servers, cars, phones and industrial equipment. It has no factories of its own.
customers: Data centre and server makers, carmakers, industrial equipment manufacturers and consumer electronics firms.
money: power delivery for AI servers and data centre equipment
power chips for vehicles, factory equipment and networking
moat: Proprietary process technology that puts more of the power circuit on a single chip, giving smaller and more efficient parts that are designed into products years ahead.
risks: AI server power delivery is concentrated among a few large customers
Most manufacturing and testing is done in Asia, mainly China, which carries political risk
Semiconductor demand outside data centres has been weak
The shares trade at a high multiple of earnings
opportunities: Revenue grew about 26% in the last financial year on AI server demand
It holds about $1.1 billion of cash and almost no debt
Each new server generation needs more power conversion content per rack
watch: Enterprise data revenue and whether it wins sockets in the next AI server platform.
